post.author: Christine Gwinnup
post.body:
Welcome to Ault, a quaint town where history and community spirit thrive together. In Weld County, Colorado, Ault proudly bears the nickname "A Unique Little Town." With an elevation of 4,938 feet and a growing community that reached 1,519 residents as of the 2010 census, Ault offers a refreshing escape from the bustling city life.

A History Steeped in Trails and Rails

Ault's historical roots are deeply entwined with the Trappers' Trail, once a bustling thoroughfare for miners, soldiers, and settlers. As the town developed, it became a pivotal crossroads for agriculture, primarily due to the efforts of Alexander M. Ault, who in 1893 established a grain and cattle business alongside the newly laid tracks of the Union Pacific Railroad. This strategic move marked the beginning of Ault's significance as an economic hub for Northern Colorado's agricultural industry.

Honoring Heroes and Heritage

The heart of Ault beats strong with pride for its heroes and heritage. Liberty Park, a central feature in town, honors Congressional Medal of Honor and Purple Heart recipient Pfc. Joe P. Martinez. His bravery during World War II is immortalized with a statue that stands as a reminder of the town’s rich historical tapestry.

Living in Ault Today

While agriculture once dominated its economy, today Ault has diversified. It now hosts various businesses and services, from banking and retail to the headquarters of the Highland School District. The town has also become a bedroom community for those working in nearby cities like Cheyenne, Fort Collins, and Greeley, making it an ideal location for those seeking tranquility without sacrificing convenience.

The Future of Ault

As Ault continues to grow, residents and officials are proactive in shaping its future. A comprehensive plan developed by the community will guide land use and development, ensuring that Ault retains its unique character while embracing necessary changes.

Main Attractions and Recreation

  • Pawnee National Grassland: Just steps from Ault, this natural prairie landscape is perfect for hikers, bird watchers, and nature lovers. Explore the Pawnee Butte Trail or enjoy a quiet picnic amidst stunning rock formations and vibrant wildflowers.
  • Antique Shopping: Ault's main street is lined with delightful antique stores, offering treasures and trinkets for every taste.

Annual Celebrations

  • Fall Festival: Every August, this festival brings the community together to celebrate with food, fun, and festivity.
  • International Food Fest: Held in late September, this event delights the senses with international cuisines, live entertainment, and activities for all ages.

Exciting New Addition: Bad Bitch Cellars

Ault welcomes Bad Bitch Cellars, a boutique winery founded by two dynamic women who turned their passion for wine into a thriving business. Specializing in custom-made wines, they offer a personal touch to every bottle, celebrating the spirit of Ault with every sip. Located conveniently near local eateries like Pizza Plus, Grey's Cafe, and Cinn Station, the winery adds a sophisticated flair to Ault’s dining and drinking scene.

Dining in Ault

  • El Dorado Mexican Grill: Serving up authentic Mexican cuisine that's become a local favorite.
  • Pizza Plus: Perfect for family dining or a quick, delicious slice.
  • Grey's Cafe: Known for hearty breakfasts and homestyle cooking.
  • Cinn Station: Don't miss their famously indulgent cinnamon rolls, a must-try for sweet tooth aficionados.

Visit Ault

Whether you’re exploring the historical sites, enjoying local cuisine, or participating in community events, Ault offers a blend of old-world charm and modern convenience. It's more than just a place on the map—it's a community where history, culture, and friendship are the cornerstones of life. So why not take a trip to Ault, where every visit feels like coming home? Discover the gateway to Pawnee National Grassland and experience what makes Ault, truly, a unique little town.
